mappedContracts.statement: Replace synthetic HTTP status 0 and broad status heuristics with discriminated transport outcomes and operation-specific success contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Transport results distinguish response, network-error, cancelled, timeout, and outcome-unknown.
Every operation defines allowed response codes and validates the response schema.
No network failure or redirect can be reported as success.

mappedContracts.statement: Represent lost responses after a possible mutation as outcome-unknown and reconcile before any replay.
acceptanceCriteria: A connection loss after request transmission never becomes an automatic retry or definitive failure.
The recovery path reads remote state and resolves success, failure, or continued uncertainty.
Run logs and exit codes distinguish outcome-unknown.

mappedContracts.statement: Retry mutations only when server-side idempotency is verified and actually transmitted, or when reconciliation proves the original mutation did not occur.
acceptanceCriteria: A local string is never treated as remote idempotency.
POST retries are disabled by default.
Idempotency keys are bound to an exact canonical plan and sent according to verified endpoint contracts.

mappedContracts.statement: Rate-limit policy imports may only move toward greater safety by default and cannot self-assert server provenance or confidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Imported receipts cannot shorten intervals or increase mutation retries without independently approved override.
One parser handles all Retry-After forms using an injectable clock and RNG.

mappedContracts.statement: Build a deterministic Substack protocol simulator with fake clock, deterministic RNG, request ledger, partial failures, lost responses, retries, auth expiry, schema drift, conflicts, rate limits, redirects, and zero-mutation assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: Simulator scenarios cover every read and write capability.
No CI test requires a live Substack mutation.
Fixtures are redacted, schema-versioned, and replayable.
